results.title: Most of the B200 providers I've tracked for a year raised their price, but the market median barely moved. Why? | Gene Kobilansky
highlights:
Most of the B200 providers I've tracked for a year raised their price, but the market median barely moved. Why?

A year ago the B200 was barely rentable: one provider in March 2025, three by fall. Today I track 15+ listing it on-demand. As all that supply arrived, here's the cross-provider median (on-demand, per GPU):

> Oct 2025: $4.99 (3 providers)
> Jan 2026: $4.64 (10)
> Jun 2026: $5.50 (15)

Basically flat. Now look at what individual incumbents did over the same stretch:

> Together AI: $5.50 → $11.95 (up 117%)
> Vast.ai: $2.44 → $4.23 (up 73%)
> Lambda: $4.99 → $6.99 (up 40%)
> RunPod: $7.99 → $5.98 (down 25%)
> Nebius: $5.50 → $3.95 (down 28%)

Most of the older providers I tracked raised, some a lot. So why didn't the median climb?

Simple -> new entrants.

A steady stream of providers kept showing up at the bottom of the market (Deep Infra $2.79, Packet $2.25, Vultr $2.99, GMI $4.00), and each one pulled the median back down about as fast as the incumbents pushed it up.

That's the opposite of the H100 story, where the budget tier itself nearly doubled and dragged the whole market up with it. On the B200, new supply is providing some slack.

The spread tells the rest: $2.79 (Deep Infra) at the floor, $14 (Oracle) at the top, 5x for the same card. The open question in our data is which force wins next, incumbents still nudging up or the next wave of entrants landing underneath them. I keep adding providers faster than I can keep up, so my money's on the entrants.

results.title: NVIDIA RTX A6000 Pricing (June 2026) | Beam
highlights:
An NVIDIA RTX A6000 costs $0.33 to $1.09 per GPU-hour to rent on demand from the providers below, against a market median of $0.56 across 17 providers. Beam's A6000 machine is $0.54 an hour with vCPU, RAM, and NVMe included. The A6000 is an Ampere card with 48 GB of ECC memory and NVLink support, and a cheaper route to 48 GB than the L40S.

## Key takeaways

- RunPod Community Cloud lists the lowest rate, $0.33, but getdeploying shows it out of stock. Its Secure Cloud is in stock at $0.53.
- Vast.ai's marketplace data shows offers from $0.36 and a median of $0.40, a narrow spread.
- Beam's $0.54 is $0.02 under the median, which getdeploying reports as flat over 90 days.

## RTX A6000 cloud prices per hour, by provider

| Provider | SKU | On-demand $/GPU-hr | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RunPod | RTX A6000 (Community Cloud) | $0.33 | Out of stock per getdeploying; Secure Cloud $0.53, in stock |
| Vast.ai | RTX A6000 (marketplace) | $0.36 | Cheapest rentable offer; median offer $0.40; spot from $0.13 per getdeploying; marketplace data from Vast.ai |
| Beam | A6000 PCIe | $0.54 | On-demand machine; vCPU, RAM, and NVMe included |
| Runcrate | RTX A6000 (48GB, PCIe) | $0.63 | Per-second billing; listings run up to $2.13 |
| Lambda | NVIDIA A6000 (1x, 14 vCPUs, 100 GiB RAM) | $1.09 | Same rate for 2x and 4x; out of stock per getdeploying; plus sales tax |
| Market median | — | $0.56 | Across 17 providers with an on-demand price (getdeploying) |

## How these prices were collected

Each figure is an on-demand, per-GPU list price for a single-GPU shape where one is offered, with spot rates kept to the notes. Marketplace data from Vast.ai.

- RunPod's pricing page has both cloud tiers.
- Vast.ai's GPU pricing page has the floor and median offers.
- Beam's pricing page has the on-demand machine rate.
- Runcrate's pricing page lists its A6000 rate.
- Lambda's pricing page has the 1x, 2x, and 4x rates.
- getdeploying's RTX A6000 tracker supplies the median.

...

## Where to rent an RTX A6000 for less

Two providers list the A6000 below Beam's $0.54. RunPod Community Cloud is $0.33 when it has stock, and RunPod Secure Cloud is in stock at $0.53, a cent under Beam. Vast.ai's marketplace data shows offers from $0.36, with spot capacity from $0.13 per getdeploying for interruptible jobs. Runcrate is $0.63; Lambda's $1.09 includes 14 vCPUs and 100 GiB of RAM but shows no stock.

Beam's $0.54 includes vCPU, RAM, and NVMe on an on-demand machine. Serverless billing that scales to zero covers Beam's RTX 4090 and RTX 5090, not the A6000.

results.title: RAM Price Hikes Push OVHcloud to Seek Contributions From Former Customers - Dawn Liphardt
highlights:
This form of “solidarity” appears set to take effect on April 1, 2026. The company has not issued an official announcement, but it generally mentions this date in emails sent to the affected customers.

...

The head of OVHcloud had signaled the approach a few weeks prior. Producing the same server would cost 15 to 35% more by the end of 2026 than by the end of 2025, he anticipated at the time. In this context, prices for certain Cloud products (Public Cloud, Private Cloud, and Bare Metal lines) “would increase by 5 to 10%” between April and September 2026; and this “could accelerate.”

Two weeks later, the executive had stated that RAM prices and NVMe drive prices were expected to peak around June 2026. News had just come out that Crucial was exiting the consumer market.

...

As of the latest updates, Octave Klaba no longer predicts more than a 250 to 300% increase between September 2025 and the end of 2026. More importantly, he envisages, at that same horizon, a balance point between supply and demand. He still believes prices will stay high at least until 2028, the time it will take for new memory production capacities to come online.

In response to this situation, prices in the Cloud range were expected to rise on average by 9 to 11% for hardware deployed in 2026-2028, the chief executive announced on February 20, 2026. “To compensate,” machines deployed between 2021 and 2025 would also be priced higher: +2 to +6% depending on the age of the hardware. At the same time, OVHcloud would “slightly adjust” the price of IPv4 addresses. The new tariffs would come into effect on April 1 or May 1, 2026. But they would only apply at the end of the engagement periods.

...

“ I should have said ‘a few euros or 9/11%,’” he eventually admitted in response to a French customer surprised at “raking in more than 50% increase” for a VPS subscribed at the end of 2025.

Prices for VPS are not rising only in France. In Canada, for instance, testimonies describe increases exceeding 50%, and approaching 100% in some cases. There, additional IPv4 addresses have indeed also gone up, now priced at $2.39 before tax.

Apart from VPS, the increase also affects the Advance 2024 and 2026 dedicated servers, as well as Rise-S, Rise-M, Rise-L and Rise-XL. It does not affect Kimsufi, So you Start, nor Rise-1, Rise-2, Rise-3 and Rise-4.

Octave Klaba does not hide it: spreading the costs across multiple lines, including RAM-light products, is meant to “prevent customers from finding Cloud 2026-2028 too expensive.” The catch is that more than a few are struggling to swallow the idea of raising prices on servers whose components were purchased before the price surge and have already been amortized.

...

To date, OVHcloud has not officialized anything and has not updated its public pricing. Perhaps they are taking the temperature first.

The last price increase of this magnitude in the Cloud lineup occurred at the end of 2022. It was largely attributed to energy costs, especially since a portion of OVHcloud’s procurement hedges were expiring.

In the VPS catalog, Elite servers had gone up 16%; Value 17%; Comfort 19%; Starter 20%; Essential 28%.

In the Bare Metal family, OVHcloud had applied roughly a 10% increase for Advance servers (except ADV-1), Scale (except Scale-7) and High Grade. In Bare Metal Eco, there was a +10 to +12% rise for the Kimsufi family (except KS-1), 10 to 11% for the So you Start lineup and 10% for the Rise series.

On the Public Cloud side, price increases ranged from 4 to 10% for general-purpose servers as well as RAM-focused ones; from 5 to 10% for CPU-oriented servers; and 9 to 10% for GPU-oriented servers.

Block storage rose by 7%; object storage by 10%; snapshots and backups by 13%.

results.title: Nvidia H100 and GPU Pricing 2026: Buy, Rent, and Cloud Costs Explained - by Dev To
highlights: The Nvidia H100 was the workhorse behind nearly every major language model trained between 2023 and 2025, and in 2026 it remains a central line item in any AI infrastructure budget. But H100 pricing is famously hard to pin down: there is no clean sticker price, rental rates swing widely by provider, and newer GPUs like the H200 and B200 are reshaping the value calculation. This guide lays out Nvidia H100 pricing in 2026 across buying, renting, and cloud, compares it to the rest of the lineup, and gives you a framework for the buy-versus-rent decision. Key takeaway A single Nvidia H100 80GB costs roughly $30,000 to $40,000 to buy in 2026. Cloud rentals range from about $1 per GPU-hour on neo-cloud spot capacity up to $7.50 or more on hyperscalers, with specialized GPU clouds typically 50 to 75% cheaper than AWS, Azure, or Google for the same hardware. The H200 often beats the H100 on both price and performance for memory-bound inference, so check it before defaulting to H100. How Much Does an Nvidia H100 Cost toBuy? Buying outright is a major capital expense. A single H100 80GB GPU typically runs $30,000 to over $40,000, depending on the form factor (PCIe or SXM), vendor, and market demand. Nvidia does not publish formal list prices for these accelerators, so most figures come from resellers and leaks, which is part of why small teams struggle to predict GPU costs. That price reflects what the card actually is: TSMC 4nm manufacturing, 80GB of HBM3 memory that alone costs several thousand dollars, 700W power delivery, NVLink interconnects, and full data-center validation. At the server level, an 8-GPU H100 board has been estimated around $216,000. Owning hardware also carries power, cooling, and operational overhead that belongs in any honest cloud versus on-premise comparison. Nvidia H100 Cloud Rental Pricing in2026 Renting is where most teams actually consume H100 capacity, and the spread is enormous. The representative on-demand and spot rates per GPU-hour in 2026 vary significantly by provider type. Neo-cloud spot instances start from around $1.03 per GPU-hour and are the cheapest option, though they are preemptible and best suited for fault-tolerant workloads. Specialized GPU cloud providers generally charge between $2.00 and $4.39 per GPU-hour and offer both on-demand and reserved cluster options. AWS on-demand pricing typically ranges from approximately $3.93 to $6.88 per GPU-hour, reflecting hyperscaler-grade reliability and integrations. Google Cloud is comparatively competitive among hyperscalers at around $3.00 per GPU-hour. Microsoft Azure sits at the high end, with rates around $12.29 per GPU-hour, making it the most expensive option but one that is often selected for high-availability requirements. The pattern is consistent: hyperscalers are not the cheapest option for any GPU class in 2026. The lowest rates come from neo-clouds and marketplaces, and for interruption-tolerant workloads spot pricing leads. For workloads that cannot be interrupted, on-demand rates across the specialized providers tend to sit within about 20% of each other, so regional availability often matters more than the headline hourly cost. H100 vs A100 vs H200 vsB200 The H100 no longer sits alone. Understanding where it fits against the rest of the lineup is the key to not overpaying. The A100 80GB comes with 80GB of HBM2e memory, carries a lower purchase price than the H100, and typically rents for between $1.29 and $2.50 per GPU-hour. The H100 80GB uses 80GB of HBM3 memory, costs approximately $30,000 to $40,000 or more to purchase, and rents for roughly $1 to $7.50+ per GPU-hour. The H200 increases memory capacity significantly to 141GB of HBM3e, is priced modestly above the H100 when purchased, and typically rents for between $2.30 and $10.60 per GPU-hour. Nvidia's B200 (Blackwell) offers even higher memory capacity, generally costs between $30,000 and $50,000 to buy, and rents for approximately $2.12 to $18.00 per GPU-hour. When each onewins A100 is cheaper per hour, but the H100 delivers 3 to 5x better throughput on transformer workloads via its Transformer Engine. Cost per training run, not per hour, is what matters; a faster H100 job can be cheaper overall. H200 has 76% more memory than the H100 (141GB vs 80GB) and more bandwidth, and starts cheaper per hour from some providers. For memory-bound inference, it is often the better buy on both price and performance. B200 (Blackwell) carries a launch premium on both purchase and cloud rates, but for the largest workloads it is where the frontier is heading as availability scales. Buy vs Rent: The Decision Framework The buy-versus-rent question comes down to utilization and time horizon, not the hourly rate in isolation. Rent when demand is variable, bursty, or experimental. Cloud GPUs avoid a six-figure capital outlay and let you scale up and down. Spot capacity suits fault-tolerant training and batch inference. Buy when utilization is high and sustained. For steady, near-continuous workloads over multiple years, on-premise ownership is often the most cost-effective once you account for the full multi-year total cost of ownership. Model the full TCO either way. On-premise must include power, cooling, networking, and staff; cloud must include egress and idle waste. The same discipline that governs cloud spend applies here, as we cover in our FinOps for AI token and GPU costs and cloud cost optimization guides. Where H100 Pricing IsHeading After a long period of scarcity and premiums, H100 rental rates have settled near multi-year lows, which makes 2026 a favorable time to rent rather than buy. As B200 and newer Blackwell parts become widely available, expect modest further softening on H100 rates, perhaps 10 to 20%, and small bulk-purchase discounts on the cards themselves. The practical implication is that locking into a large multi-year H100 purchase today carries more depreciation risk than it did a year ago, while flexible rental keeps your options open as the generation turns over. How to Control GPUCosts Shop beyond the hyperscalers. Neo-clouds and GPU marketplaces are routinely 50 to 75% cheaper for the same H100, so compare widely before committing. Match the GPU to the workload. Use H200 for memory-bound inference, A100 where throughput needs are modest, and reserve B200 for genuinely frontier-scale jobs. Use spot for interruption-tolerant work. Fault-tolerant training and batch inference can run on preemptible capacity at a fraction of on-demand rates. Measure cost per outcome. Track cost per training run or per million inferences, not just per GPU-hour, and attribute GPU spend to teams and projects, as covered in our cloud cost allocation guide. Conclusion Nvidia H100 pricing in 2026 is a tale of two numbers: $30,000 to $40,000 to own, or roughly $1 to $7.50 an hour to rent, with the rental market split sharply between cheap neo-clouds and expensive hyperscalers. The H100 is still the cost-effective default for large-scale training, but the H200 frequently wins on memory-bound inference and the B200 is climbing the frontier. With rates near multi-year lows and a new generation arriving, renting is the lower-risk choice for most teams, while sustained high-utilization workloads can still justify buying. Compare providers aggressively, match each GPU to its workload, and measure cost per outcome. If you want help attributing and optimizing GPU and cloud spend, that is exactly the discipline Opslyft brings.

results.title: SemiAnalysis报告：全球GPU租赁产能"卖到秋天"，H100一年期合约价涨近40%_sellbgp
highlights:
报告核心结论相当直接：截至目前，市场上所有预计在今年8月到9月之前上线的算力容量，已经被提前全部预订完毕。这种紧张程度直接反映在价格上——H100一年期GPU租赁合约价格，从2025年10月每GPU每小时1.70美元的低点起步,一路上涨近40%，到2026年3月已经攀升至每GPU每小时2.35美元。报告还提到，按需（On-Demand）模式下的GPU租赁容量几乎全部售罄，且已经锁定了按需实例的客户普遍不愿意将容量释放回公共池，即便面对持续上涨的价格也是如此。

报告援引路透社的报道指出，中国企业已经为2026年预订了超过200万颗英伟达H200芯片，而英伟达当前库存仅约70万颗，供需缺口十分明显；同时援引彭博社的消息称，受中东局势紧张影响，霍尔木兹海峡的船舶保险费用已上涨至船只价值的5%，这种地缘政治层面的连锁反应也在间接推高包括AI数据中心建设在内的整体供应链成本。

SemiAnalysis分析认为，接下来需要重点观察GB300系列集群在2026年内的产能释放节奏，以及高带宽内存（HBM）、DRAM、NAND等关键存储部件的供应紧张是否会进一步恶化，这两个变量将共同决定算力租赁价格是否会在年内见顶。

SemiAnalysis这份报告最值得关注的一点是"按需容量几乎全部售罄、且持有者不愿释放"这个细节——这意味着即便预算充足，企业也可能面临"有钱租不到"的现实困境。对于依赖GPU算力的企业用户，Sellbgp建议把【算力资源的可获得性】和【供应商的产能锁定能力】放在和价格同等重要的位置去评估，必要时可以考虑【提前签订中长期算力租赁框架协议】，而不是等到业务高峰期再去现货市场抢资源。

results.title: 【2026年6月】生成AIをクラウドGPUで安く回す：主要サービス料金比較とコスト最小化の4手
highlights:
この記事は、2026年6月時点の主要サービスの実際の料金を並べて、生成AI（とくに画像生成）を一番安く回すにはどこをどう選べばいいかを示します。価格はすべて各社公式または集計サイトから取得し、出典と取得日を末尾に置きました。クラウドGPUの価格は需給とリージョンで動くので、その前提で読んでください。

## 先に結論

個人の画像生成なら、ハイパースケーラ（AWS/GCP）のオンデマンドは割高です。コミュニティ/マーケット型のクラウドを選び、Spot価格を使い、ワークロードに合ったGPUに絞る。この3つでオンデマンドの数分の1になります。

SDXLのような画像生成はVRAM 24GBあれば十分です。ここがコスト判断の起点になります。

## 24GB級GPUの料金比較（SDXLの主戦場）

2026年6月時点・1時間あたり。RunpodはCommunity Cloud、AWSはus-east-1の値です。

| サービス / GPU | VRAM | オンデマンド | Spot / Community |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AWS g6.xlarge（L4） | 24GB | $0.805 | $0.385（Spot） |
| AWS g5.xlarge（A10G） | 24GB | $1.006 | $0.435（Spot） |
| Runpod L4 | 24GB | — | $0.39（Community） |
| Runpod RTX A5000 | 24GB | — | $0.27（Community） |
| Runpod RTX 4090 | 24GB | — | $0.69（Community） |
| Lambda A10 | 24GB | $1.29 | — |
| GPUSOROBAN（A4000〜・国内/円建て） | — | ¥50/時〜 | — |

同じL4でも、AWSオンデマンドの $0.805 に対しRunpod Communityは $0.39。ほぼ半額です。そしてAWSのSpot $0.385 はRunpod Communityとほぼ同じ。最初の分岐は「コミュニティ型を使うか、Spotを使うか」です。

速度がほしいならRunpodのRTX 4090（$0.69）が画像生成では扱いやすい帯。とにかく単価を下げたいならA5000（$0.27）や、Vast.aiのマーケット最安帯という選択になります。Vast.aiは需給で価格が動くマーケットプレイス型で、最安だが時価という性格です。

## 大型モデル・LLM向け（80GB級）

70B級のLLMや動画生成で大きなVRAMが要るなら、桁が変わります。

| サービス / GPU | VRAM | 1時間 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runpod A100 | 80GB | $1.39〜1.49 |
| Lambda A100 | 40GB | $1.99 |
| Runpod H100 | 80GB | $2.89〜3.29 |
| Lambda H100 | 80GB | $4.29 |

画像生成にこの帯は普通は不要です。24GB級とH100では時間単価が数倍から10倍ほど違うので、H100を借りてSDXLを回すのは、そのままコストの取りこぼしになります。

...

### 1. GPUを盛りすぎない

いちばん効くのに、いちばん見落とされがちなのがこれです。SDXLにVRAM 80GBは要りません。24GB級で足ります。自分のワークロードに必要なVRAMを先に決めてから、GPUを選ぶ。順番を逆にすると、過剰なスペックに毎時間払い続けることになります。VRAMの目安は別記事「ComfyUIのVRAM不足を直す判断フロー」も参考にしてください。

### 2. オンデマンドよりSpot / Community

AWSのL4はオンデマンド $0.805 がSpotで $0.385。およそ半額です。生成バッチのように「途中で止まっても再実行できる」処理はSpotと相性がいい。常時起動のAPIサーバなど、中断が困る用途だけオンデマンドにします。

### 3. 秒・分単位課金で、アイドルを止める

最大の無駄は借りっぱなしです。Runpodは秒単位、GPUSOROBANは分単位で課金されます。生成が終わったらインスタンスを止める。これを徹底するだけで、月額は大きく変わります。クラウドのコストは「単価×時間」で、多くの人は単価ばかり見て時間を放置しています。

### 4. ドル建ての為替も計算に入れる

Runpod・Lambda・Vast.aiはドル建てです。円安が進むと、同じ $0.39 でも円換算の実コストは上がります。国内のGPUSOROBAN（円建て・A4000で1時間50円〜、公称でAWS/GCP/Azure比およそ半額）は、為替を気にしたくない人や、請求を円で完結させたい人の選択肢になります。

...

ここまでは「借りるときに安くする話」でした。一歩引くと、GPUを買うのとクラウドで借りるの、どちらが安いのかという問いが残ります。答えは使用量で変わります。月に数時間なら借りるが圧勝、毎日何時間も回すなら買ったほうが早く元が取れます。

...

価格は需給・リージョン・時期で変動します。下記は取得日 2026-06-12 時点の各社公式または集計サイトの数値です。

- Runpod（Community Cloud）: https://www.runpod.io/pricing
- Lambda: https://lambda.ai/service/gpu-cloud
- AWS（ vantage.sh 集計・us-east-1。原典はAWS公式 https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand/ ）
- GPUSOROBAN: https://soroban.highreso.jp/
- GCP（具体額はリージョン依存・公式を参照）: https://cloud.google.com/compute/gpus-pricing
- Vast.ai（時価・マーケットプレイス）: https://vast.ai/pricing

results.title: AI Infrastructure Costs: Controlling Enterprise GPU Spending-OneSource Cloud
highlights:
### GPU Compute

GPU compute is the single largest cost driver in AI infrastructure. The price per GPU-hour varies significantly by GPU model, acquisition method, and provider. As of mid-2026, NVIDIA H100 SXM cloud rental rates span from approximately 2.50perhouronspecializedGPUprovidersto 2.50 p er h o u ro n s p ec ia l i ze d GP U p ro v i d ers t o 6.50 or more per hour on major hyperscalers. H200 GPUs with 141GB HBM3e memory command premium pricing but can serve larger models on fewer GPUs, potentially reducing per-inference cost despite higher per-GPU rates.

GPU pricing has been volatile. After declining through late 2025 as supply caught up with demand, H100 one-year lease contract prices rose approximately 40 percent over five months into early 2026, driven by massive inference demand from proliferating open-source models and production AI deployments. This volatility itself is a cost planning challenge — organizations that budgeted based on late-2025 pricing found their projections outdated within months.

The acquisition model determines whether GPU costs are capital expenditure or operating expenditure. On-demand cloud rental charges per hour with no commitment, suitable for variable or exploratory workloads. Reserved or committed-use contracts reduce hourly rates by 24 to 75 percent in exchange for one-to-three-year commitments. Spot or preemptible instances offer the deepest discounts — 60 to 90 percent off on-demand — but carry interruption risk that makes them unsuitable for production inference.

### Public Cloud GPU Rental

Public cloud GPU rental offers near-zero upfront cost and rapid deployment — instances can be provisioned in hours. For exploratory workloads, short-term projects, and burst capacity, this model is cost-effective. But for sustained production workloads, costs scale linearly with usage. An 8-GPU H100 cluster running at 70 percent utilization on a major hyperscaler at 5perGPU−hourcostsapproximately 5 p er GP U− h o u rcos t s a pp ro x ima t e l y 2.5 million annually in compute alone, before storage, networking, and operations.

This model eliminates egress surprises, provides predictable performance on non-shared hardware, and typically costs less per GPU-hour than on-demand cloud for sustained workloads.
